osaka_menya_75hz_kuromon.notes: [Ramen · 24-hour Takaida-style shoyu ramen by Kuromon] A cramped ten-seat counter by Kuromon Market serving Takaida-style ramen around the clock; it's closed only Thursdays and the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays. Reviewers call the brand "7.5Hz" or "Nanahan". The bowl is a rich, sharp soy broth with more acidity than one visitor expected, thick straight noodles with low moisture, and chashu, best with an extra heap of chopped green onion. One reviewer who knows the original Takaida shop found the same chashu and noodles here, with a slightly milder broth. Chuka soba is ¥800 and a large chashu ramen ¥1,100 (September–October 2026). There's a garlic spice on the counter. People drop in after a night out, or for a morning bowl at 8 am. One person works the shop at a time, and a service charge may be added.

chef_bio.background: A Kuromon branch of the Takaida-style ramen shop Menya 7.5Hz (September 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "While the service differs from the Takai-da branch, the basic concept remains the same. The flavor of the chashu is identical, and the noodles taste the same as well. However, the broth seems slightly milder here." — September 2026.
"The broth, which had a stronger acidity than I expected. The noodles were straight and had a low moisture content." — October 2026, late night, chuka soba with green onions.

Touch-panel ticket machine at the entrance; noodle firmness asked when you hand over the ticket (September 2026). No reservations. Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_tenchijin_ramen_2gouten.notes: [Ramen · light tonkotsu shoyu beside Nankai Namba] A 16-seat counter right beside Nankai Namba Station, open since 2019 and good value. Every ramen here is pork-bone based, and though it looks rich and fatty it eats surprisingly light, with a depth of dashi and medium-thick noodles that soak it up. Generous crunchy green onions add to that. Say how firm you want the noodles when you hand over your ticket. Pickled ginger from the counter works well with the tonkotsu. The ramen-and-pork-bowl set is ¥1,280 (September 2026), and the pork is stir-fried after you order. There's also abura soba (¥1,000) with three slices of chashu, spicy meat mazesoba that can sell out, and tsukemen with a free large size. One diner found it a bit salty. Tabelog only says it opens at 11:00, so check closing times.

chef_bio.background: Second branch of Tenchijin Ramen (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Light tonkotsu shoyu ramen; pork bowl.

anecdotes.text: "At first glance, it looks like it would be rich and fatty, but surprisingly, it was light and easy to eat—delicious! The noodles were medium-thick and absorbed the broth well." — October 2026, second visit.

"The broth was a bit lighter, but it had a rich tonkotsu flavor with a nice depth from the dashi… the combination of tonkotsu and ginger was fantastic." — September 2026, original-flavor ramen and pork-bowl set ¥1,280.

osaka_hard_romanticker_namba.notes: [Standing bar · a Tabelog 100 tachinomi with no sign, behind Namba] A small standing bar just off Midosuji near Namba Hips, named to Tabelog's 2025 standing-bar 100 and a sister of Oishi Stand. There's no sign, so it's easy to walk past; the shop's Instagram says to look for it. It gets packed; one evening a regular shuffled over to make room. Reviewers note many women among the crowd, unusual for a tachinomi. Small plates make it easy to try a lot. The cream cheese with crackers, slightly sweet, won over one reviewer who doesn't usually like cream cheese, and the blue cheese has fans too. There's Shine Muscat with prosciutto as shira-ae, an Ezo venison steak served rare, and house satsuma-age with cheese, corn and edamame, fried after you order. A hamburger is limited to three servings. Expect ¥2,000–4,000. Cash only. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Sister shop of Oishi Stand (August 2026 review); Tabelog tachinomi 100, 2025 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: House-made dishes, down to the satsuma-age (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "On Instagram, it said, 'There's no sign, so please find us,' and I actually walked past it without realizing it! The small interior was packed. A regular customer kindly moved to make space for me." — October 2026.

osaka_kokopelli_namba.notes: [Burgers · American burgers and world beer by Hozenji] A stylish American-style burger bar a few steps from the Hozenji entrance, open since 2011 and drawing overseas guests too. The toasted buns get singled out; one burger hunter ranked it in a personal top three, buns especially. The cheeseburger is ¥1,480, plus ¥350 for a drink (July 2026). The bacon cheeseburger layers thick bacon over a juicy patty, and the avocado burger is creamy and rich. The tender pulled pork with an addictive barbecue sauce looks as good as it does on Instagram. A macaroni-topped burger has been on TV. The grilled-cheese sandwich comes on toasted whole-wheat bread with thick bacon and avocado, and the chef adjusted the cheese on request. The fries are crisp without being greasy. There's a long list of bottled beers from around the world. Lunch is burgers only. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: American-style burger and beer bar by Hozenji Yokocho (Tabelog); official site kokopelli-nanba.jp.

anecdotes.text: "I've been to various famous burger joints, but this one ranks in my top three for taste, especially the buns, which might be the best I've ever had." — July 2026, cheeseburger ¥1,480.

osaka_gendai_kappou_hozenji_momo.notes: [Japanese · a hidden creative kappo by Hozenji Yokocho] A creative kappo counter with private rooms, tucked deep inside a nondescript building by Hozenji Yokocho, open since 2021. Finding the door takes some effort. The kitchen builds colorful courses on Japanese seasonal tradition. Lunch is the easy way in: a weekday mini course with seasonal clay-pot rice for ¥3,000, or ¥5,000 for more. Recent courses ran from a lotus-root dumpling in vivid broccoli sauce to fried sanma served as a salad, with crispy okra among the starters. The clay-pot rice, chestnut in autumn or corn, scallop and shiso in summer, leaves enough for seconds, and what's left is made into rice balls to take home. Several diners praise the tableware and care. One critic found the dishes pre-plated and the egg rice hard and clumped. Dinner runs about ¥8,000–15,000. Closed most Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Contemporary kappo with jazz music and private rooms (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Creative dishes rooted in Japanese seasonal tradition but not limited to it (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The chestnut rice, cooked in a clay pot, was so delicious that even after a second helping, there was still some left." — October 2026, ¥5,000 lunch course; the rest was made into rice balls to take home.
"Most of the dishes are pre-cooked (essentially prepared in advance) and served already plated." — October 2026, a critical review.

Reservations accepted; at dinner, groups with children are seated in a private room. A 5% year-end fee applies 15 December–4 January (Tabelog). Cards, QUICPay, PayPay and Alipay accepted.
osaka_teppanyaki_zin_namba.notes: [Teppanyaki · Kobe-beef teppanyaki with a Dotonbori night view] A 14-seat teppanyaki counter on the eighth floor above Yoshinoya, looking out over the lights of Dotonbori. The head chef came up through luxury hotels (reviewers name the St. Regis Osaka and the Ritz), and the cooking shows it. You choose black wagyu, Matsusaka or Kobe beef for the omakase. A 14-course black-wagyu strip loin course was ¥12,000 (April 2026), and an anniversary course with tenderloin ¥16,000. Beyond the steak, diners rave about the seafood: crisp-skinned sea bass with shiso genovese, and teppan-fried Nagasaki horse mackerel with a pickle tartar, one diner's best ever. Wagyu dumplings in consommé and seared wagyu sushi round it out, and rice cooked in a kamado from Kyoto's Gihei closes the meal. One diner found the seasoning a little salty. Many guests are from abroad; the menu is in English and staff speak English.

chef_bio.background: Head chef trained in hotel kitchens, previously at the St. Regis Osaka and the Ritz (July 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Some dishes run a food-cost ratio above 40% (July 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The pan-seared sea bass and fried horse mackerel, finished on the teppan, had a delicate flavor reminiscent of French cuisine. I learned that the head chef trained at a hotel." — July 2026.

"I opted for the 14-course OMAKASE featuring Black Wagyu Strip Loin for JPY 12,000, along with a wine pairing of 5 selections for JPY 4,400… it was fully booked with foreign guests aside from us." — April 2026.

osaka_nipponbashi_sakaichi.notes: [Ramen · a six-seat morning-ramen counter in Shimanouchi] A six-seat counter in Shimanouchi, rated 3.64 on Tabelog, open since 2022 and run by the owner with one helper. It opens at 7 am on weekends, and lines can form outside by 8. The regular menu is shoyu: a chicken and seafood broth that's easy to drink to the last drop, chewy flat whole-wheat noodles from Menya Teikaku, and in the Shoyu Special (¥1,600) four kinds of chashu, from low-temperature chicken breast to hanging-roasted pork belly. The fun is the rotating bowls announced on social media. Recent ones included a cement-gray niboshi soba from Himi sardines that is clean, with no bitterness, a clear niboshi-and-scallop shio, a thick crab-and-scallop shio, and a tachiuo tsukemen with a raw-egg kamatama dip. Choose the house kombu-water tsukemen or the rich chicken-and-seafood one (¥1,200 with an ajitama, October 2026). There's also a special rich shrimp version with sakura shrimp and a spicy tamago tsukemen. Squeeze sudachi or lime over the noodles near the end. One diner missed a soup-wari to thin the rich dip, which isn't offered. Expect a 20–30 minute line at weekend lunch. The crowd skews to visitors from abroad.

osaka_yakitori_midori_hozenji.notes: [Yakitori · a 1958 yakitori counter by Hozenji] A 12-seat L-shaped counter a few steps from Mizukake Fudo in Hozenji Yokocho, grilling yakitori since 1958. The second- and third-generation owners now run it together and keep the old flavors. Chicken from Ise Akadori, shamo and Tajima birds goes over Kishu binchotan. The tare is just soy sauce and sake, rich and smooth with no extra sweetness, and diners say it lets the chicken speak. First-timers must take a course (Matsu, Take or Ume; one group paid ¥6,000 a head for a course in September 2026) and can order à la carte afterward. Expect negima, chicken breast with shiso and ume, the house Midori-yaki, chicken skin, "tulip" wings and stuffed shiitake, with onsen egg and yamakake on the side. Check sake prices, which add up fast. One September diner found the meat tough and the hygiene off-putting. Book ahead; closed Sundays.

The signature (¥820, September 2026) arrives as one serving split into two small bowls, a nod to a married couple, and ordering it as a couple is said to bring luck. Don't share: it's one order per guest. The zenzai is made with Tanba Dainagon azuki, gently sweet and a little thick, with a few whole beans and a soft rice-cake dumpling. Salt kombu and green tea cut the sweetness, and staff refill the tea. In summer there's a chilled zenzai, plus matcha-azuki kakigori. Today it's run by the Wasyoku Sato group and open 10 am to 10 pm, handy for dessert after takoyaki. There's a shelf of Meoto Zenzai souvenirs.

There are surprises, like kiwi tempura. Dip in matcha salt, yuzu salt or tentsuyu with grated daikon, and the staff will suggest which. You can also order à la carte. The chef is cheerful and chatty. Upstairs, the shop's sake bar AWA pours a wide range of sake and whisky for after. Closed Wednesdays.

The all-you-can-drink courses are good value (¥2,750 with three dishes in April 2025, ¥4,950 with skewers and sashimi in March 2025). osaka_menya_joroku_namba.notes: [Ramen · Takaida-style black chuka soba, a Tabelog 100 regular] A seven-seat counter down a narrow alley near NGK, named to Tabelog's ramen 100 every year from 2017 to 2025, with lines and a waiting area at lunch. It opened in 2008 at Tempozan Marketplace and moved to Namba in 2010. The chuka soba is Takaida-style: a broth that looks nearly black and smells strongly of soy, yet drinks lighter and less salty than you'd expect, with black pepper on top. Medium-thick straight noodles soak it up, with thin chashu, menma and green onion. A small is ¥900 and a regular ¥1,000 (October 2026). Add the ¥200 hayazushi, vinegared rice wrapped in leaves from Wakayama. There's also a shrimp shio with sakura shrimp and niboshi, limited bowls such as a garlic ramen on special days, and on the first Sunday of the month it opens at 7 am for morning ramen. A Hokkaido visitor found the soy too assertive. Cash only; closed Wednesdays.

The basic Japanese-style ramen (¥880, April and September 2026) is a mild shoyu on chicken and pork bones with medium straight noodles, a thick slice of chashu, menma, nori and plenty of white and green onion. It's crowd-pleasing rather than distinctive. One regular prefers the tsukemen, with a lighter-than-usual dip, thinner noodles and thick, chilled pork-belly chashu. The pork rice bowl is a favorite but isn't served late at night. Sides are just ramen toppings (¥150), and drinks just canned beer (¥400). The ticket machine sends your order straight to the kitchen, so food comes fast. Open every day.

osaka_takoya_kukuru_souemoncho.notes: [Takoyaki · a sit-down Kukuru takoyaki shop by the Dotonbori river] A basement branch of the well-known Kukuru takoyaki chain on the Souemoncho side of the Dotonbori river, with 20 seats so you can eat sitting down instead of queuing at a street stall. Buy a ticket at the machine out front and wait for your number, which can be hard to hear. The takoyaki come fast off a very hot griddle: fluffy outside, gooey and piping hot inside, with decent pieces of octopus. Ask for extra mayonnaise and aonori if you like. The largest order is 12 pieces, and there's a takoyaki-and-beer set served in a cute octopus-shaped tray. It's busy with visitors from abroad, and one diner found the service a little perfunctory. Open daily 11 am to 6 pm.

chef_bio.background: Kukuru takoyaki chain, with shops in Kanto as well (August 2026 review); official site dotonbori-kukuru.com.

anecdotes.text: "Freshly made, they were piping hot, so I waited about 3 minutes before taking a big bite. The outside was fluffy while the inside was gooey! And there were decent-sized pieces of octopus inside." — August 2026, 12 pieces.
"I bought a ticket from the vending machine in front of the shop and ordered a lemon sour and takoyaki. I took my order to a table in the back." — August 2026.

osaka_sumibi_yakitori_ainosuke_dotonbori.notes: [Yakitori · binchotan yakitori in a Dotonbori basement] A basement yakitori bar on Dotonbori's main street, open since 2016, grilling fresh chicken over binchotan. Dinner starts with a ¥385 bowl of grated daikon that's refilled for free. The signature is chicken-thigh tataki (¥858), crisp skin over a rare, tender center. Skewers start at ¥297, and the neck, skirt and liver get the praise, along with heart, wings and vegetables like shiitake and cherry tomato. Don't skip the wing-tip kara-age in three flavors: soy, sweet-spicy yangnyeom and tartar nanban. Finish with the rich grilled rice ball under egg yolk and shaved cheese, or a yakitori ramen with a whole skewer on top. The menu comes in English, Chinese and Korean. Open nightly until midnight.

osaka_teppan_osaka_souemoncho.notes: [Teppanyaki · casual wagyu teppanyaki in Souemoncho, open to 3 am] A 19-seat teppanyaki counter opposite Queens Court in Souemoncho, open since 2020 and serving until 3 am. The star is a limited domestic black-wagyu filet; in July 2026 it was an A5 chateaubriand, seared on the teppan and rested to medium-rare with rosemary; an August diner had it with mashed potatoes. Beyond steak there's wagyu ichibo roast beef, Hokkaido scallop and asparagus in butter soy, a seafood yakisoba, Camembert fondue and white fish with Genoa sauce. Courses add a truffle-scented salad and a pairing of sirloin cap and filet, with wasabi, salt, soy, garlic chips and truffle oil to dip. Reviewers spent ¥5,000–15,000. The shop says on Tabelog that it can handle allergies and vegetarian requests, so say what you need when booking. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Casual teppanyaki in Souemoncho (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Selected ingredients at reasonable prices; allergies and vegetarian options accommodated (Tabelog).

osaka_yakiniku_hiromiya_souemoncho.hours_raw: Mon–Sat and holidays 18:00–2:00 am; closed Sunday (by arrangement) and irregularly (Tabelog). Reservations strongly advised with only five seats (2019–2024 reviews). Smoking allowed (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted. English menu (Tabelog).
osaka_yakiniku_hiromiya_souemoncho.notes: [Yakiniku · a five-seat yakiniku counter in a Souemoncho alley] A five-seat yakiniku counter tucked into a narrow Souemoncho alley, cramped enough that you'll be elbow to elbow, and the kind of casual, affordable solo spot that's getting rare in Minami. A new owner took over in 2025, and a returning diner in July 2026 felt the meat had improved since the change. Everything comes in half portions, so one person can work through salted tongue, cheek, premium loin and kalbi. Omasum, tetchan intestine and liver have fans too. Ask about the off-menu ajillo, grilled rice balls and miso pasta, and finish with fried rice or cold noodles. Expect about ¥3,000–5,000. Book ahead. Smoking is allowed. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: New owner from April 2025 (August 2025 review); "the manager changed" (July 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "This was my first visit since the manager changed. Everything was served in half sizes… I felt like the quality of the meat has improved." — July 2026.
